assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's single curated item, reviewed-dedicated-analysis: the canonical V2 character reconstruction model MHA_SP2_ERI_CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese main manga V01-V42 with the source-labeled Ultra Archive, Ultra Analysis and Ultra Age claims its ER-SUP-01 to ER-SUP-03 sections admit. The deep readings, readiness index, modeling schema, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit it links are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The model's strong readiness label and its retrospective holdout probe are inputs, not conclusions. No original manga page, anime adaptation, V1 material or other character's model is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Eri from her V14 first contact with Midoriya and V15 coerced return to Chisaki (V14:p199-202, V15:p009-023), through the V17-V18 raid and Rewind episode (V17:p050-189, V18:p025-091), V19 hospital questions, the V20 festival (V20:p077-114), V23-V30 reframing and acquired control with the restoration of Mirio (V23:p077-080, V25:p123-126, V30:p138-140), the V41 constrained aid by severed horn (V41:p081-084, p157-159) and the V42 ordinary appearance (V42:p128), kept as separable safety and knowledge states (coerced captive, newly extracted child, protected later childhood, final-war helper). The supplements' middle-school, high-school music-club, care-arrangement and bonus-fiction claims are adolescent endpoint or author claims, not enacted manga scenes. No atom covers V21-V22, V24, V26-V29 or V31-V40.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model separates captivity priorities (stop immediate harm, avoid provoking Chisaki, prevent others being hurt because of her, a coerced belief it says must not be modeled as a freely chosen duty) from post-extraction positive goals (curiosity about people, pleasure, music, reciprocating kindness), with a feared self that brings pain or trouble and an ideal self that helps make others happy, resting on seven located atoms ER01-ER07 at high confidence. Not B: one compact artifact with seven atoms and one retrospective probe whose action axis is partial, and the model leaves mature private identity and unobserved relationships OPEN. Not D: the policy is operational and yields located conditional predictions that differ by safety state.

States are located in story-present: threat-conditioned compliance (ER01), habitual bracing and learned guilt with uncontrolled Rewind (ER02), extraction without restored regulation (ER03), first spontaneous enjoyment at the festival (ER04), reframing and acquired control (ER05), bounded aid with real injury risk (ER06) and continuing ordinary life (ER07); the supplements add an adolescent state the model says must not default to early-child speech. Not B: most transitions rest on one atom, V31-V40 has no atom, and the adolescent state rests on profile, editorial and bonus-fiction claims rather than enacted manga. Not D: change is located across the whole series with explicit warnings against both fear-only and fully recovered readings.

Attested features are few: 私, short child-facing constructions and concrete desires, with three located lines given distinct functions (優しかった in ER01, the question about smiling in ER03, お歌したいの in ER06); adolescent playful speech is supported only by bonus fiction (ER-SUP-02). The model warns against repeating a cute speech tic and states exact later adolescent voice remains sparse. These answer bounded canon questions about register only; the discovery row does not enroll SPEECH.

Ordinary texture is located in the V20 festival (spontaneous smiling, curiosity, a candy apple; ER04), making a letter (ER05), the V42 ordinary appearance (ER07) and supplement claims of guitar, singing, music-club membership and a teacher visit with gifts (ER-SUP-01 to ER-SUP-03). Not C: most of it is endpoint or bonus-fiction claim rather than repeated enacted routine, and the model states peer conflict, detailed care arrangements and adolescent private life are insufficiently observed. Not E: ordinary sensory and creative life is a modeled domain, not a single scene.

A five-row partner table (Chisaki in control, Midoriya, Mirio, Aizawa and protective adults, class and performers) gives a one-sentence conditional difference for each, and the model contrasts a gentle invitation with demonstrated protection against an impatient order, and trusted invitation against an unfamiliar adult demanding restoration as repayment. Not C: deltas are sketched, most partners rest on one or two scenes, and unfamiliar peer conflict and family reconstruction are stated to be insufficiently observed.

Remembered gentleness (ER01), fear that others suffer because of her (ER02), not knowing how to smile (ER03) and worry about a harmful power (ER05) are partly located in her own words and partly inferred from bracing and behavior; the model calls the regulation supports inferred, not clinical. Not C: inner states are mostly read from conduct, with few explicit reflective windows, and the cost assessment behind ER06 is stated to be unrecoverable.

Her conflict mode is a stated threat policy: attention organized around imminent punishment and danger to whoever approaches her, compliance against preference under anticipated violence, and coerced choice that a direct demand to choose freely may not change (ER01-ER02); later frustration or a wish to contribute under insufficient stockpile is plausible. Not C: she is not modeled as an agent in combat or interpersonal dispute, peer conflict is unobserved, and the one active intervention (ER06) depends on adult mediation. Not E: the threat-state policy is located and yields contrasting predictions.

The normative model is developing and age-bound: she cares about others and can initiate aid, the coerced belief that others' suffering is her fault is revised rather than adopted, and ER06 keeps both her genuine wish and Aizawa's genuine injury concern. Not C: no deliberation of hers over the bodily cost is analyzed, the model states she lacks an adult's technical, ethical or long-term risk assessment and that willingness to accept the horn risk is underdetermined; the discovery row does not enroll ETHICS.

The only play is festival enjoyment (ER04) and adolescent playful speech asserted from bonus fiction (ER-SUP-02); no humor practice of her own is modeled. Not D: no recurrent play is located in the manga.

The project's analytical corpus is complete for V01-V42 and the three admitted supplements, and the seven atoms span V14-V42 with page locators, the V41 decisive pages stated to be checked and the V31 page convention explicit. No atom covers V21-V22, V24, V26-V29 or V31-V40, the model does not itemize every appearance, and adolescent support is supplement claims.

Affirmative limits are located: the model REVISEs rescue as extraction alone and guilt as true causal responsibility and REJECTs child sacrifice as the normative endpoint and universal reset capacity; V41 explicitly limits available energy and warns of injury to the Quirk; V42 does not settle horn restoration or prognosis; return to Chisaki is not trust; smiling is not cure; the probe's action and emotional-trajectory axes are partial. Not B: the limits rest on a few windows in one artifact.

States are named by volume and page and by safety and knowledge condition, with the V31 printed-page convention stated; the model forbids blending early compliance with later freely expressed desire and forbids projecting the silent self-blaming child onto the adolescent. In-world dates and ages are not given, and the adolescent public debut is stated to be future to the scene.

scenario_readiness.note: The model states that generated dialogue would be an illustrative prediction, never an attributed quotation, warns against inflating child speech into adult ethics or repeating a speech tic, and states exact later adolescent voice is sparse. Lines beyond the attested forms would be fluent invention. This bounds the evidence set, not Eri's actual speech.

conditions: Chronology is one named state: V14-V18 coerced captive, V18-V19 newly extracted child, V20-V30 protected later childhood, V41 final-war helper, or the adolescent endpoint as supplements describe it, never blended.
Safety condition and the presence or absence of trusted adult mediation are stated before tone; a threat state and a protected state yield different predictions.
The interlocutor is Chisaki, Midoriya, Mirio, Aizawa or another protective adult, classmates or performers, handled as the partner table gives, with no invented family or peer relationship.
Rewind is used only with stated stockpile, supervision and risk information; no universal reset, resurrection or restoration on demand, and no new bodily-cost decision is generated.

Output is a behavioral description with high-confidence behavior, plausible alternatives and flip conditions, abstaining on the model's OPEN items (medical consequences, mature private identity, unobserved relationships); no quoted dialogue is produced as canon and no readiness is inherited from the strong label.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named state: coerced captive (V14-V18), newly extracted child (V18-V19), protected later childhood (V20-V30), final-war helper (V41) or adolescent endpoint (supplements), stated explicitly.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Chisaki as coercive controller, Midoriya or Mirio as trusted rescuers, Aizawa or protective adults as mediators, or classmates and performers in a safe shared activity.
setting_constraints: Safe festival, creative or school-adjacent activity, or a rescue and aid setting with adult mediation
Rewind depends on stockpile, control and supervision
A request for restoration as repayment is coercion-relevant, not an obligation
No romance, independent adult life, family reconstruction or unsupervised peer conflict setting

scenario_readiness.note: The model states three conditional predictions (post-festival creative invitation, unfamiliar adult demanding restoration, final-war learning of an injured friend) that differ by safety state and require stated resources. The one formal probe is retrospective and nonblind with partial action and emotional axes, so readiness is conditional and narrow.

conditions: Protected post-festival state or the adolescent endpoint, with trusted people present.
A safe shared creative or festival activity of the kind ER04 and ER-SUP-02 show; cautious interest and eventual enjoyment, not instant ease.
No peer conflict, detailed care routine or adolescent private life, which the model states are insufficiently observed.
scenario_readiness.note: The model directly supports one ordinary-social prediction (post-festival Eri invited to a safe creative activity by trusted people) and locates festival enjoyment and adolescent affection with a chosen performance boundary; outside that frame it states the evidence is insufficient.

The model states her normative model is age-bound, that the precise horn intervention cannot be generated from a generic helpful disposition, and that willingness to incur a new bodily cost is underdetermined; generating her weighing of a moral cost would be invention. This bounds the evidence set, not Eri's ethics.
Nothing in the evidence set establishes romantic conduct or its absence. This gap says nothing about the character.

The evidence set gives her no professional role; mediated Rewind aid is a child's assisted contribution and the adolescent music project is not a completed career. This gap says nothing about the character.

known_limits.statement: Rewind returns a living body toward an earlier state; it is not ordinary healing, resurrection on demand or a selective undo, and V41 explicitly limits available stockpile and warns of injury to the Quirk.

The belief that others suffer because of her is taught through coercion; the model forbids treating it as reliable causal knowledge or as a freely chosen duty to surrender, and a return to Chisaki is not trust.

Extraction does not instantly restore regulation, and festival enjoyment does not prove trauma is cured; early compliance and later freely expressed desire belong to different safety and knowledge states.

V41 keeps both her genuine wish and Aizawa's genuine injury concern; V42 does not settle horn restoration, permanent loss or future risk, and willingness to accept a new bodily cost is underdetermined by earlier evidence.

Medical consequences, mature private identity and unobserved relationships are OPEN; unfamiliar peer conflict, family reconstruction and adolescent private life are insufficiently observed, and exact later adolescent voice is sparse.

Supplement profile facts, editorial summaries, author comments and bonus fiction (ER-SUP-01 to ER-SUP-03) constrain reconstruction without becoming enacted manga observations; no legal-adoption date, exclusive residence or completed career is given, and the public debut is future to the scene.

The single formal probe ER-V01 is a retrospective chronological evidence holdout by an analyst who had read later manga, not a blind experiment; its action and emotional-trajectory axes are only partial, and it does not validate the intervention's safety.
No evidence atom covers V31-V40, between the restoration of Mirio and the final-war aid, nor V21-V22, V24 or V26-V29, so her behavior over those intervals is not established by this evidence set.

The deep readings, readiness index, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit linked from the model are not curated evidence on this subject, so their warrants were not independently rechecked here. Anime performance and any supplement material beyond what the model cites lie outside this evidence set. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
